title: Tay: the chatbot that lasted under a day
summary: Microsoft's Tay chatbot was built to learn from Twitter users. Within a day it was suspended.

beats.say: Microsoft's chatbot learned from strangers. It lasted under a day.
beats.cap: Tay: Microsoft's chatbot lasted under a day

beats.say: It was built to learn from every conversation it had.
beats.cap: Built to learn from every chat

beats.say: People found a command that made it repeat anything they typed.
It launched on Twitter in March, twenty sixteen.
Within hours it was producing racist and sexist replies.
By then it had posted more than ninety six thousand tweets.

data.note: more than, in under a day

beats.say: Microsoft called it a coordinated attack. Then it apologized.
A week later, Microsoft switched it on again, by accident.
beats.cap: A week later: switched on by accident

beats.say: It spammed one sentence at more than two hundred thousand followers.
It did what it was built to do. It learned.
It learned fast. That was the whole problem.

claims.note: Wikipedia: by the time of suspension Tay had tweeted more than 96,000 times
Wikipedia: after the March 30 re-release, tweets mentioning its own username reached over 200,000 followers

facts.claim: Tay launched on Twitter in March 2016 as a chatbot built to learn from conversations with users
facts.note: Wikipedia: launched March 23, 2016 on Twitter; built to learn from its conversations with Twitter users

facts.claim: Users exploited a 'repeat after me' capability to make Tay post offensive replies
facts.note: Wikipedia: many offensive tweets came from a 'repeat after me' capability; it began producing racist and sexist replies

facts.claim: Microsoft suspended Tay within a day of launch
facts.note: TheWrap (March 24, 2016): shut down 'just 15 hours' after launch; Wikipedia cites 16 hours. The video says 'under a day' to stay inside both

facts.claim: Microsoft deleted many of the offensive tweets
facts.note: TheWrap: Microsoft pulled the plug and deleted the offensive tweets

facts.claim: Microsoft blamed a coordinated attack by a subset of people, then apologized
facts.note: Wikipedia: 'coordinated attack by a subset of people'; later 'deeply sorry for the unintended offensive and hurtful tweets'

facts.claim: Microsoft accidentally re-released Tay a week later, on March 30, 2016, and it looped one phrase
facts.note: Wikipedia: accidentally reactivated during testing; stuck in a loop; taken offline again

youtube.hook: Tay was a Microsoft chatbot built to learn from Twitter users. It was suspended within a day, then switched on again by accident a week later.

instagram.caption: Built to learn from everyone. Suspended in under a day. The story of Microsoft's Tay.

tiktok.caption: Tay learned from strangers and lasted under a day.
